intro.say: Animals belong to groups. Let's look at fur, feathers and fins!

rounds.say: Mammals have fur or hair. Mammal mums feed their babies milk. Cows, dogs and cats are mammals.
rounds.caption: Mammals: fur and milk

rounds.say: Birds have feathers and wings. Fish live in water. They swim with fins and breathe with gills.
rounds.caption: Birds: feathers · Fish: fins

options.label: Dog
options.why: A dog has fur, not feathers.

options.label: Fish
options.why: A fish has shiny scales.

rounds.explain: A duck is a bird, and all birds have feathers.

rounds.ask: Which animal swims with fins and breathes with gills?

options.label: Cat
options.why: A cat breathes air with lungs. It does not have gills.

options.label: Bird
options.why: Birds breathe air with lungs.

rounds.explain: Fish use fins to swim and gills to breathe under water.

rounds.ask: This animal has soft fur and drinks milk as a baby. Which group is it in?

options.label: Bird
options.why: Birds have feathers, and a rabbit has fur.

options.label: Fish
options.why: Fish live in water and have fins.

rounds.explain: A rabbit has fur and drinks milk, so it is a mammal.

rounds.ask: Sort the animals: fur or feathers?
rounds.explain: Furry animals are mammals. Feathery animals are birds.

options.label: Mouse
options.why: A mouse has fur, so it is a mammal.

options.label: Fish
options.why: A fish has fins, not wings.

rounds.explain: A rooster has feathers, wings and a beak. It is a bird!

intro.say: Let's meet three more groups: reptiles, amphibians and insects.

rounds.say: Reptiles have dry, scaly skin. Most reptiles lay eggs. Snakes, lizards, turtles and crocodiles are reptiles.
rounds.caption: Reptiles: dry scales

rounds.say: Amphibians, like frogs, have smooth wet skin. They start life in water as tadpoles. Insects are tiny and have 6 legs.
rounds.caption: Amphibians: wet skin · Insects: 6 legs

options.label: Frog
options.why: A frog has smooth wet skin. It is an amphibian.

options.label: Rabbit
options.why: A rabbit has fur. It is a mammal.

rounds.explain: A turtle has dry scaly skin and lays eggs, so it is a reptile.

options.label: Lizard
options.why: A lizard has dry scales. It is a reptile.

options.label: Bee
options.why: A bee has 6 legs. It is an insect.

rounds.explain: A frog has wet skin and starts life as a tadpole in water.

rounds.ask: How many legs does every insect have?

options.why: Count again: insects have 3 legs on each side.
8 legs is a spider, and spiders are not insects.

rounds.explain: All insects have 6 legs: 3 on each side.
rounds.hint: Count 3 legs on each side of the ant.

rounds.explain: Reptiles have scaly skin. Insects are tiny with 6 legs.

rounds.ask: A crocodile has dry, scaly skin and lays eggs. Which group is it in?

options.label: Mammal
options.why: Mammals have fur and feed babies milk.

options.label: Amphibian
options.why: Amphibians have wet, smooth skin.

rounds.explain: Dry scales and eggs mean a crocodile is a reptile.

intro.say: Some animals look like they belong in one group, but really belong in another. Let's be animal detectives!

rounds.say: A whale lives in the sea, but it is not a fish. It breathes air through a blowhole and feeds its baby milk. It is a mammal!
rounds.caption: Whales and dolphins are mammals

rounds.say: A bat can fly, but it has fur and drinks milk, so it is a mammal. A penguin cannot fly, but it has feathers, so it is a bird.
rounds.caption: Bat: mammal · Penguin: bird

rounds.ask: A dolphin swims in the sea, breathes air and feeds its baby milk. Which group is it in?

options.label: Fish
options.why: Fish breathe with gills, but dolphins come up for air.

options.label: Reptile
options.why: Reptiles have scales and most lay eggs.

rounds.explain: Breathing air and feeding babies milk makes a dolphin a mammal.

rounds.ask: Which of these animals is a mammal that can fly?

options.label: Eagle
options.why: An eagle has feathers. It is a bird.

options.label: Butterfly
options.why: A butterfly has 6 legs. It is an insect.

rounds.explain: A bat has fur and feeds its babies milk, so it is a flying mammal.

rounds.ask: A penguin cannot fly. Why is it still a bird?

options.label: It swims
options.why: Fish and seals swim too, so that is not the clue.

options.label: It lives in the cold
options.why: Polar bears live in the cold, and they are mammals.

rounds.explain: Only birds have feathers, so a penguin is a bird.
rounds.hint: Think: what do all birds have?

rounds.ask: Sort these sea and sky animals into their groups.
rounds.explain: Whales, dolphins and bats are mammals. Penguins and swans are birds. Sharks and clownfish are fish.

rounds.ask: A shark lives in the sea and breathes with gills. Which group is it in?

options.label: Mammal
options.why: Mammals breathe air, but sharks use gills.

options.label: Amphibian
options.why: Amphibians have wet skin and start as tadpoles.

rounds.explain: Sharks breathe with gills and swim with fins, so they are fish.

rounds.ask: Which clue tells you an animal is a mammal?

options.label: Lays eggs
options.why: Birds, reptiles and fish lay eggs too.

options.label: Lives in water
options.why: Fish and frogs live in water too.

rounds.explain: Only mammals feed their babies milk. That is the best clue.
